# @oidfed

> OpenID Federation for JavaScript and TypeScript: trust-chain discovery and validation, metadata policies, Trust Marks, constraints, OIDC registration, and wallet roles. The five libraries use standard Web APIs and share a test suite across Node.js, Deno, Bun, workerd, Electron, and Chromium. Their runtime dependencies are `jose` and `zod`.

@oidfed implements the [OpenID Federation 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-1_0.html) trust framework and related specifications listed below. Its endpoint handlers accept a standard `Request` and return a `Promise<Response>`. Applications connect them to an HTTP server or worker and supply persistent storage and key-provider implementations.

## Packages

- [@oidfed/core](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/packages/core/README.md): Federation primitives — entity statements, trust chain resolution and validation, metadata policy, JOSE operations, typed schemas, caching, and trust marks. Foundation for every other package.
- [@oidfed/authority](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/packages/authority/README.md): Trust Anchor and Intermediate Authority operations: subordinate management, statement issuance, and federation endpoint handlers, including fetch, list, resolve, Extended Listing, Subordinate Events, and Entity Collection.
- [@oidfed/leaf](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/packages/leaf/README.md): Leaf Entity toolkit — Entity Configuration serving, authority discovery, and trust chain participation for any entity at the edge of a federation (typically RPs or OPs that don't issue subordinate statements).
- [@oidfed/oidc](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/packages/oidc/README.md): OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 federation flows — automatic and explicit client registration, Request Object validation, and typed RP/OP metadata processing as defined in OpenID Federation 1.0 §12.
- [@oidfed/wallet](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/docs/packages/wallet.md): Wallet Provider, Credential Issuer, and Credential Verifier roles, federation trust checks, JWT Wallet Attestations, and protocol-engine integrations.

## Tools

- [@oidfed/cli](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/docs/tools/cli.md): Command-line interface for inspecting, validating, and debugging OpenID Federation deployments: resolve trust chains, decode entity statements, verify signatures, check trust mark status, generate keys, sign statements, and query listing, collection, and event endpoints. Install with `npm i -g @oidfed/cli`.

## Apps

- [@oidfed/home](https://oidfed.com): The authoritative @oidfed site — project intent, ecosystem, about. Machine-readable overview: <https://oidfed.com/llms.txt>.
- [@oidfed/explorer](https://explore.oidfed.com): Visual federation-exploration tool — inspect entity configurations, trace trust chains, browse metadata, validate topology. Browser-based, no backend. Machine-readable overview: <https://explore.oidfed.com/llms.txt>.
- [@oidfed/learn](https://learn.oidfed.com): Interactive OpenID Federation 1.0 course — 15 lessons from first principles to federation topology design. Machine-readable overview: <https://learn.oidfed.com/llms.txt>.

## Documentation

- [Wiring Guide](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/docs/guide/wiring-guide.md): End-to-end integration with Express.js and `panva/node-oidc-provider`. Worked eduGAIN-topology example covering Trust Anchor, Intermediate, OP, and RP.
- [Storage Guide](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/docs/guide/storage-guide.md): Production storage adapters, authority namespaces, subordinate records and event histories, Trust Marks, collection snapshots, replay protection, and the separate federation key-provider boundary.
- [Dev Guide](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/docs/guide/dev.md): Running the full multi-topology federation locally with wildcard DNS and TLS.
- [E2E Test Infrastructure](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/docs/test/e2e.md): Integration harness — real HTTPS over undici + Express + `oidc-provider`.
- [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): Setup, test commands and runtime coverage, commit conventions, and the PR process.
- [SECURITY](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/SECURITY.md): Vulnerability disclosure policy.

## Related Specifications

- [OpenID Federation 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-1_0.html) *(final)* — this library's target spec. **Implemented.**
- [OpenID Federation 1.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-1_1.html) *(final)* — protocol-independent successor layer (Entity Statements, Trust Chains, Metadata, Policies, Trust Marks, Federation Endpoints). **Implemented** by virtue of 1.0.
- [OpenID Federation for OpenID Connect 1.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-connect-1_1.html) *(final)* — protocol-specific layer (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC entity types, client registration). **Implemented** by virtue of 1.0.
- [OpenID Federation Extended Subordinate Listing 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-extended-listing-1_0.html) *(draft 03)* — paginated subordinate listing with audit timestamps and bulk per-entity claim retrieval. **Implemented** end-to-end (server, client, CLI).
- [OpenID Federation Subordinate Events 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-subordinate-events-1_0-01.html) *(draft 01)*: signed authority histories, core verification, and CLI retrieval. Event storage is optional; authority lifecycle operations capture changes transactionally.
- [OpenID Federation Entity Collection 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-entity-collection-1_0.html) *(draft 01)*: implemented in core. Authorities and leaves can serve the endpoint. Supports explicit snapshot refresh, filters, informational metadata, language selection, and CLI queries.
- [OpenID Federation for Wallet Architectures 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-federation-wallet-1_0.html) *(draft 05)*: implemented in `@oidfed/wallet` with composable provider, issuer, and verifier roles, JWT Wallet Attestations, and federation-backed request validation. Applications supply VCI/VP protocol engines and credential-format verification.
- [ACME with OpenID Federation 1.0](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-acme-openid-federation/) *(IETF Internet-Draft)* — Federation Entity Types for ACME Requestor / Issuer roles; automated X.509 over federation discovery. Not yet implemented.

## Federation Operator Notes

Running a federation involves responsibilities beyond what this library enforces. Operators must read and address OpenID Federation 1.0 §17 (Implementation Considerations — multi-path ambiguity, Trust Mark policy design, resolver/TA co-location), §18 (Security Considerations — DoS prevention, `authority_hints` depth limits, Trust Mark filtering, reverse-proxy end-to-end signing), and §19 (Privacy Considerations — minimising personal data, short-lived Trust Mark Status tokens). This library provides the protocol mechanisms; policy, rate limiting, key management, HSM integration, and operational hardening are the operator's responsibility.

## Security

Report vulnerabilities to <dah.kenangnon@gmail.com> — see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/Dahkenangnon/oidfed/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for the full disclosure policy. Do not open public GitHub issues for security reports.
